facts.Current degree: BJMC / B.A. Journalism & Mass Communication – Podcasting / Audio / Digital Storytelling

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build programme samples and apply for radio production assistant, broadcast intern and audio production roles.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Focus on news, music programming, talk shows, community radio, sports or audio documentaries.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Progress toward senior producer, programme manager, commissioning producer or audio content lead.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine editorial judgement, audience understanding, multiplatform production and responsible use of new audio tools.

blocks.text: Learn to plan, script, record, edit and coordinate radio programmes that inform and entertain listeners, from live news bulletins and interviews to music shows, community programmes and podcasts.

blocks.label: Course-to-career mapping
blocks.text: Radio Producer is closely aligned with the course’s audio and digital storytelling focus. The exact official taxonomy role list could not be independently verified, so treat the match as provisional.

blocks.label: Timeline assumption
blocks.text: This roadmap uses 2026–2030 as a four-year planning horizon. If your degree is three years, complete the core production portfolio and internship milestones by graduation; use the final-year items as optional extensions.
These are planning outputs;
Year-by-year plan

rows.text: Learn radio formats, audience needs, programme rundown structure and basic audio recording.
Produce a 2-minute spoken segment with a script and rundown.
Practise microphone technique, voice links, interviews and audio editing.
Deliver a 5-minute programme with clean transitions and credits.
Build a programme plan with timings, presenter links, interview questions and a contingency plan.
Submit a 15-minute show rundown and recorded pilot.
Learn music selection, rights checks, segment pacing, audience calls and production coordination.
Produce a 10–15-minute show with documented music and asset permissions.
Produce a news, talk, music or community programme with a clear editorial brief.
Complete a pilot with a script, rundown, source notes and feedback.
Practise live or simulated-live production, cue sheets, timing and backup procedures.
Run a 20-minute mock broadcast without missing a scheduled segment.
Coordinate a small production team and manage guest bookings, recordings, edits and approvals.
Deliver a three-episode series with a production calendar and handover notes.
Complete an internship or capstone and prepare a producer’s portfolio.
Portfolio with two full programmes, a rundown, a short showreel and references.

blocks.label: Four-year honours variant
blocks.text: If your university offers a four-year honours route, use the additional time for an industry placement, an original series, audience research or advanced broadcast production. Confirm your institution’s duration and credit requirements.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Build strength in editorial judgement, production budgeting, audience research and team management. As radio expands across streaming, apps and podcasts, learn to adapt programmes to different platforms without losing clarity, accessibility or editorial standards.

Career progression

blocks.label: Years 1–2
blocks.text: Student Producer → Years 2–4: Radio Intern / Production Assistant → Years 3–6: Assistant Programme Producer / Junior Audio Producer → Years 6–10: Radio Producer / Podcast Producer → Years 10–15: Senior Producer / Programme Editor → Years 15–20: Programming Manager / Head of Audio → Years 20+: Broadcast executive, independent production-house owner, consultant or educator.
These are indicative experience ranges, not guaranteed promotion dates. Progress depends on programme quality, audience response, editorial judgement, production budgets and leadership experience.
PhD routes
A PhD is not necessary for most radio production jobs. It may suit a research or academic career.

blocks.label: Broadcast and media studies
blocks.text: Research radio history, public broadcasting, programming or media policy.

blocks.label: Audience research
blocks.text: Study listening habits, audience engagement and digital audio adoption.

blocks.label: Sound studies
blocks.text: Research sound culture, oral histories and audio storytelling.

blocks.label: Digital media and communication
blocks.text: Study podcasting, platform distribution and changing audio consumption.
Check each university’s eligibility, available supervisors, research requirements and funding conditions.

2040–2046: staying relevant. Develop the editorial and management skills to oversee multiple programmes, mentor producers and manage budgets. As radio content increasingly reaches audiences through streaming, podcasts and digital platforms, keep learning distribution, accessibility, audience analytics and responsible AI-assisted production.
